dedupe_keys.name: community resilience estimates cre including cre for puerto rico hazard ranking tables and cre for response

description: The Community Resilience Estimates (CRE) of the U.S. Census Bureau measure how socially vulnerable every neighbourhood in the United States is to the impacts of disasters, as the share of residents with zero, one-to-two or three-plus of ten risk factors: poverty, caregivers in the household, crowding, communication barrier, unemployment, disability, no health insurance, age 65 or over, no vehicle access and no broadband internet. The 2024 CRE, released on 29 January 2026, model 2024 ACS 1-year microdata with population estimates, and for the first time rank every county and tract by social vulnerability for each natural hazard with at least a relatively moderate expected loss in FEMA's National Risk Index (winter weather, flooding, hurricane, strong wind, wildfire, earthquake), with estimates for metropolitan areas too. The CRE for Puerto Rico uses restricted Puerto Rico Community Survey microdata for the commonwealth, municipios and tracts; the CRE for Response adds variables for Disaster Impacted Population Profiles in FEMA preliminary damage assessments. Coverage: nation, states, core-based statistical areas, counties and census tracts; annual since 2019. Access: CSV files, ranking tables, the CRE Viewer, data.census.gov and the Census Data API; free, public domain. Caveats: estimates are modelled small-area estimates with margins of error; the hazard ratings come from the March 2023 National Risk Index release. Simulation uses: social vulnerability weights for resilience and risk models, prioritising restoration and emergency response. Related records: FEMA National Risk Index, CDC/ATSDR SVI, CRE for Heat, My Community Explorer and ACS tables.
